display.purpose: the page title only (Characters, Playthroughs, a character's name, the player's name on a playthrough's Overview).

headline.purpose: the selected item's name in the details pane, and the app name in the top bar.

title.purpose: category links in the sections column and the tabs under a character.

body.purpose: table cells, values, prose. Long text in the pane runs at line-height 1.6 with a 65ch measure.

label.purpose: column heads, group headings, definition terms in caps, the playthrough and game-state labels, and the theme switch.

file.purpose: a whole file as stored, in the raw bio editor and earlier versions.

shadows.name: modal-lift
shadows.purpose: Only for the quick-find dialog, which floats over the page; its backdrop is rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45).

motion.name: fly-in
motion.purpose: A short fly-in (6px rise, 180ms). In the code it plays on the details pane's content each time the selection changes, on every list screen (memory and diary tables included).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, every transition and animation is instant.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: the sections column becomes a horizontal row under the top bar, the pane stacks below the table with a top rule, and less important columns hide.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: wide columns drop, two-column overview grids stack, and the memory and diary panes narrow to minmax(18rem, 22rem).

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: The Playthroughs list widens to 90rem so its table and pane sit side by side; under max-width 90rem a filter bar takes the pane's width too.

narrative.overview:
Hermaeus is one more menu of the game you just closed. Every screen is a categories column, a sortable item table, and a full-height details pane, set on smoked glass with hairline rules and driven from the keyboard. It deliberately refuses the admin-dashboard default of gray sidebar, cards, and a blue button: there are no cards, no filled surfaces beyond the details pane, and only one more color, copper, kept for what the player changed.

The world is dense and quiet. Text is Jost at a compact 15px with tabular figures so counts, times, and importance scores line up in columns; anything that labels rather than reads (categories, headings, column heads, keys, and buttons) is set in tracked, uppercase Barlow Condensed. The accent is scarce and means "this is selected" or "this is what you can do". Dark mode is the game's near-black menus; light mode is the same world in pale smoke, built from one token set with the same roles.

The signature is the bottom button-hint strip: every hint is a real keyboard shortcut, and clicking the hint does the same thing. The SVG diamond marks the selected row, as it does in the game.

The mark is the eye of Hermaeus Mora among his tentacles (`assets/`). In the top bar it sits before the wordmark in the text color, with the eye cut out so the ground shows through; as the app icon and favicon it is verdigris on the game's near-black, in a rounded square, with a tighter frame on the eye at 16 pixels.
keyCharacteristics: Smoked-glass ground: a fixed radial gradient from a lighter smoke heart to the ground color.
Hairline 1px rules (two strengths) instead of boxes, cards, or shadows.
Tracked condensed caps for labels; Jost for reading text; tabular figures everywhere.
One accent for selection and action, and for the group headings that sort lists into sections.
Item table plus a sticky, full-height details pane that sizes itself to end at the hint strip.
A fixed bottom hint strip of live keyboard shortcuts, right-aligned like the game's button hints.

rules.name: The Changed Rule
rules.body: Copper means one thing: the player changed this from what SkyrimNet ships. It marks the thing itself (the copy, the value), never the action on it, and never doubles as a warning; a warning stays amber.

rules.name: The Scarce Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent marks selection, action, and group headings that sort a list into sections. It never fills a surface larger than a button and never decorates. If something is in the accent color, it is selected, actionable, or a heading inside a list.

rules.name: The One Token Set Rule
rules.body: Light mode is the same roles with different values, never a different design. A new color ships as a dark/light pair or not at all.

rules.name: The Label Versus Read Rule
rules.body: Anything that labels is tracked condensed caps; anything that is read is Jost in sentence case. Counts beside a label switch back to Jost with no tracking.

rules.name: The Lined-Up Figures Rule
rules.body: Tabular figures are on at the body level. Numeric columns align right.

rules.name: The Template Markup Rule
rules.body: A prompt or bio shows its Inja markup set apart from its prose: statements (`{% if %}`, `{% block %}`) in the accent, since they're the structure that acts; expressions (`{{ npc.name }}`) in a heavier ink, since they're what gets filled in; comments muted and italic; strings muted; delimiters muted. Prose stays as it is. The same marks show while the text is edited.

rules.name: The Clipped Text Rule
rules.body: Text cut short with an ellipsis shows its whole self in a tip beneath it when the pointer rests there: the pane's material with a hairline edge, lifted by a soft shadow, never the browser's own tooltip. Text that fits shows nothing.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separate with a 1px rule, never a box or a shadow. Use `rule` between rows and shell zones, `rule-strong` under column heads and group headings and around controls.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Doors Rule
rules.body: When a stat list's rows are the page's navigation (the Overview's Stored list), each name is a title-size caps link, muted at rest, beside a 1.25rem marker column. The diamond and the `select` haze mark the row the arrow keys reach; hover and focus move them, and Enter opens it, with the hint naming the row. Where a table beside it owns the arrow keys (the Playthroughs preview), the rows are plain links with no marker.

dos: **Do** put every list in the item table with a diamond column and a details pane beside it.
**Do** register a real keyboard shortcut for every primary action and let the hint strip show it.
**Do** set labels in tracked Barlow Condensed caps and reading text in Jost, with tabular figures.
**Do** separate with 1px hairlines (`rule`, `rule-strong`) and keep corners at 3px.
**Do** define every new color as a dark and light pair in the same token set.
**Do** keep the details pane opaque and sized to end at the hint strip.
donts: **Don't** use cards, gray sidebars, filled tiles, or a blue (or any second) accent color.
**Don't** use the accent for decoration or large fills; it means selection, action, or a list's group heading.
**Don't** add shadows to rows, panes, or the shell; the only shadow is the floating quick-find dialog.
**Don't** show a hint in the strip that isn't backed by a working shortcut.
**Don't** make a group label as bright as the current section.
